rules.rationale: This equation defines the proof-local numericVal predicate as the disjunction of the existing Int and Float sort predicates; it introduces a named domain summary and does not add a separate mathematical fact.
This is the base equation of the structural numericVals recurrence, defining the empty value sequence to satisfy the numeric-domain predicate.
This is the cons equation of the structural numericVals recurrence, defining a sequence to be numeric from its head predicate and recursively defined tail predicate.
This sort-specific equation defines positiveNumeric on Int values using the supplied comparison-domain terms gtF and intToF.
This sort-specific equation defines positiveNumeric on Float values using the supplied gtF comparison term.
This guarded default equation completes the total definition of positiveNumeric by assigning false exactly outside the Int-or-Float domain.
This simplification equation is the base case of the filterPositive recurrence: filtering no remaining elements returns the accumulator unchanged.
This simplification equation is the positive-head case of the filterPositive recurrence, defining the summary by appending the head and recurring on the structurally smaller tail.
This simplification equation is the nonpositive-head case of the filterPositive recurrence, defining the summary by skipping the head and recurring on the structurally smaller tail.

This simplification rewrites the pre-existing operational applyCmp symbol to the proof summary positiveNumeric over a guarded dynamic Val domain, so it is an additional cross-symbol fact rather than a defining clause. Stage 1 proves related Int- and Float-specialized connection claims, but it does not first prove this exact generic V:Val rule with its numericVal guard; the rule therefore remains in the trusted domain-lemma boundary.
